To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fecal material produced by copepods and by 3 relatively larger macrozooplanktons (2 salp spp. and a pelagic crab) contained different carotenoid patterns.

the carotenoid composition of phytoplankton pigmentation in feces of 2 different size classes of macro zooplankton grazes is different, with large grazers producing polar carotenoid hydrolysis products and smaller grazers producing intact carotenoids.
the fecal material from large macrozooplkancton grazers contained polar carotenoids, tentatively identified, as the ester hydrolase products of peridinln, fucoxanthln, and 19'hexanoylovyfucoxanthin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of carotenoid alteration products in fecal material produced by different size classes of macro zooplankton grazcrs.

the characterization of the chemical alteration of phytoplankton pigmentation by macrozooplankters and the implications of these alterations for the use of pigments as biomarkers for phytoplankton and zooplankton production.
the fate of pigments in the marine food web.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the feces produced by macrozooplanktons contain altered pigments which may provide a'signal' to indicate the presence of fecal material in the water column and sediments.
the feces produced by the large macrozooplkanon grazers contain altered carotenoids, while those of the small copepods do not.

the feces produced by macrozooplanktons are a source of carotenoid pigments to the water column and that the carotenoid composition of these feces can be used as a tracer for the presence of fecal material produced by specific size classes of macrograzers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the feces of macrozooplantkton grazers can be used as indicators of the grazing impact of the animals, and that feces of the larger grazers can be differentiated from those of smaller grazers by their carotenoid composition.
the fecal pellets of the 3 large macrozooplantkton grazers contained the ester hydrolysates of peridinin and fucoxanthin and the 19'-hexa-noyloxyfucoxantin.

the carotenoids in fecal pellets are a mixture of intact carotenoids and carotenoid degradation products, and the ratio of intact to altered carotenoids depends on the size and type of macrozooplakton grazers and the phytoplankton assemblage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fecal material produced by macrozooplank ton grazers can be used to trace the presence of these grazers in the environment.
the fecal material produced by large macrograzers is different from that produced by small macrograzers, and that the difference is related to the gut physiology of the grazers.

fecal pigments are a useful tool for identifying fecal pellets in sediment trap samples, which is important because fecal pellets are an important component of marine snow, a key contributor to carbon sequestration in the ocean.
